passage: I said it in the middle of dinner: "I'll see you all in court." I'm Tushar, and I'm not proud of it. Then I stopped answering calls from my aunt, my cousins, even Manoj, my brother. I thought silence would make them take me seriously. Instead, everyone dug in. Manoj posted a message to the family group listing what he would never give up. Dadi asked to see us both, her voice shaking, and I refused. Months later the house is still shared on paper and empty in every way that matters. There is no talk of settlement now. Every time I imagine one, I can't picture how we would get from here to sitting at one table.

qa.q: What did Tushar say in the middle of dinner?
qa.a: Tushar said, "I'll see you all in court."

qa.q: What does Tushar's remark "I'm not proud of it" suggest about how Tushar feels?
qa.a: It suggests Tushar feels regret and some shame about the threat and the silence that followed.

qa.q: What could Tushar do now to move things forward?
qa.a: Tushar could reach out to Dadi and the family, apologise for the threat, and ask for a calm meeting with a neutral elder.

qa.q: How might Dadi have felt when the brothers refused to meet?
qa.a: Dadi was probably distressed and helpless, as her shaking voice suggests.

grounding: Tushar threatens court and stops speaking to relatives, positions harden, an elder is distressed and settlement seems further away.

passage:
I live across the corridor from the Rao family, and I've known Jahnavi since college. When her grandfather's flat came up for division, she was sure her aunt was cheating her. At the second family meeting I heard her through the door: "Fine. You'll hear from my lawyer." Then the door slammed.
After that she stopped answering her aunt's calls and stopped coming to Sunday lunch at her grandmother's. The aunt, who had been ready to give way on the balcony room, hired her own lawyer. Last week I met Jahnavi's grandmother on the stairs, holding the rail, eyes swollen. She asked me, "Is Jahnavi eating properly? She doesn't come any more."
I don't know if Jahnavi regrets it. She says she is standing up for herself. But nobody in that family is talking now, only their lawyers.
— Tenzin

qa.q: What did Jahnavi say before the door slammed?
What might Jahnavi be feeling, from what Tenzin sees?
qa.a: She seems to feel wronged and angry, sure her aunt was cheating her, though Tenzin can't tell whether she has any regret.

qa.q: What could Jahnavi have tried instead of threatening court?
qa.a: She could have asked for the papers to be checked or for a neutral elder to mediate, keeping talks open while her worry was looked into.
Her grandmother is distressed, with swollen eyes, worried whether Jahnavi is eating, and missing her at Sunday lunch.

grounding: It shows a relative threatening court and cutting off contact, so positions harden, an elder is distressed and settlement slips further away.

passage:
Monday, 10 March. Damini hangs up on her uncle mid-sentence. "He thinks he can keep Dadaji's orchard because he lives nearby? I'm sending a legal notice," she tells her flatmate, Afreen. Afreen says, "Maybe sleep on it?" Damini doesn't.
Friday, 21 March. The notice has reached Shimla. Damini's uncle has blocked her number. Her cousins have left the family group. Dadi calls Afreen's phone because Damini isn't picking up, her voice shaking: "Tell her we can talk. Please."
Sunday, 13 April. The uncle has hired his own lawyer and says he will not meet until the court decides. The offer he made in February, dividing the orchard by rows, is off the table. Damini sits on the balcony with a copy of the notice, not reading it.

qa.q: What offer had the uncle made in February?
What might Damini be feeling on the balcony on 13 April?
qa.a: She may feel stuck and regretful now the offer is gone, though she was sure of her anger in March.

qa.q: What could Damini have done on 10 March instead?
qa.a: She could have taken Afreen's advice to sleep on it and then asked for a calm family meeting before any legal step.

qa.q: How is Dadi affected by the escalation?
qa.a: Dadi is distressed and pleading, calling Afreen with a shaking voice just to reach Damini.

grounding: It shows a young woman escalating with a legal threat, after which contact stops, positions harden, the grandmother is distressed and a settlement moves away.
